title: SlopCodeBench
finding: Agents extending their own code over evolving specs: erosion and verbosity rise in most trajectories; quality prompts lower starting level but not the rate of decay
numbers: 36 problems/196 checkpoints, 15 agents; best passes 14.8% checkpoints; erosion up in 77%, verbosity up in 75.5%; agent code 2.3x more verbose, 2.0x more eroded than 473 OSS repos; prompt guidance cuts initial verbosity/erosion up to 1/3, no effect on degradation slope

title: Evaluating AGENTS.md
finding: Repo context files do not generally improve task success; raise cost; overviews unhelpful; instructions followed; useful for non-standard practices
caveats: measures issue resolution, not design quality

title: Not All Agents Are Equal
finding: Quality vendor-specific; pooled agent code has fewer security smells than human
numbers: 37,623 PRs, 2,807 repos; Codex revert 6.1% vs human 11.5% (OR 0.50); Devin 14.5% (OR 1.31); security smell OR 0.63
sample_or_setup: AIDev dataset, 5 agents vs matched human baseline
caveats: selection effects in what PRs agents get; preprint

title: Post-merge quality in agent bug-fix PRs
finding: Raw SonarQube issue-count differences vanish after normalizing by churn; merge success not a reliable quality signal; code smells most common
sample_or_setup: from search summary only, abstract not fetched

title: GitClear AI Copilot Code Quality 2025
finding: Cloned lines up, moved/refactored lines down 2021-2024
numbers: cloned 8.3%->12.3% of changed lines; moved ~25%->under 10%; 211M lines
sample_or_setup: commit data Jan 2020-Dec 2024; vendor of analytics tool
caveats: correlational, AI usage not directly labelled; vendor

title: Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail
finding: 14 failure modes in 3 categories (system design, inter-agent misalignment, task verification); gains over single-agent often minimal
caveats: no per-mode rates read; no controlled single vs multi comparison

title: Anthropic multi-agent research system
finding: Multi-agent beat single agent on internal research eval; ~15x tokens vs chat; coding has fewer parallelizable tasks
sample_or_setup: internal eval, research task not coding

title: Empirical evaluation of agent frameworks on code tasks
finding: 7 frameworks compared; effectiveness moderate; AgentOrchestra coordination overhead; no clean single-vs-multi test in abstract
caveats: search summary claimed single-agent ahead on repair; not verified

title: Cross-context review of LLM output
finding: Fresh-session review beats a second same-session review; not significantly better than a single same-session review
numbers: 30 artifacts, 150 injected errors; F1 CCR 28.6 vs SR2 21.7, SR 27.1, SA 23.8
caveats: small; v2 retracted run-1 advantage; injected errors not natural defects

title: Agentic Property-Based Testing
finding: Agent writing Hypothesis PBTs found real bugs in popular packages
numbers: 100 packages; 56% valid bug reports, 32% reportable; top-21 86% valid; 5 reported, 3 patches merged
caveats: bug finding in existing code, not compared to example-based tests or to agent-authored product code; vendor authors

title: Rethinking value of agent-generated tests
finding: Changing how many tests agents write did not significantly change SWE-bench Verified outcomes; tests mostly print statements
caveats: agent self-written tests during issue fixing, not human-first TDD

title: TDD for code generation (TGen)
finding: Providing tests with the problem raises success
numbers: abstract gives no figures; GPT-4, Llama 3; MBPP, HumanEval
caveats: human-supplied tests; function-level not design quality

title: METR RCT
finding: Experienced devs 19% slower with AI, believed 20% faster

title: No measured evidence found for architecture/design-doc-up-front effect on design quality
finding: Only unverified blog-reported constraint decay (~30pt) and ContextCov tool paper
